title.narrative: Multi Threat EarlyWarning System

description.narrative: The project’s goal is to reduce the vulnerability and risk of the Dominican Republic to multiple threats (e.g. flooding, fires, landslides, etc.) based on effective and timely information, improving its evidence-based decision-making process and its effective communication to the population. This goal will be achieved by enhancing and building enabling elements and information elements:1.Strengthen and expand Dominican Republic’s early warning system framework to allow the development of early warning systems and reduce losses and damages to civil society and infrastructure2.Enhance Dominican Republic’s real-time decision-making capacities based on information tools3.Streamline the delivery of timely information and messages on incoming threats to the general population to reduce their exposure and reduce their vulnerability.

This proposal for the Strengthening of the Early Warning System seeks to enhance capacities to increase the precision and dissemination of warnings to the population in the event of extreme disasters. To achieve this, three action components are proposed (a) Design of a multi-hazard EWS, (b)Development of the National Risk Atlas (NRA) and (c) Strengthening of "COE Alerts". These three components present an integral vision and a long-term response that would contribute to the mitigation of atmospheric effects and climate change in the country. A) Design of a multi-hazard EWS: The aim is to achieve a more comprehensive, clear and articulated EWS approach, by providing information with a higher level of detail, indicating the recommended reaction to be adopted by the population in case of the issuance of an alert, in such a way that they act proactively and protect their lives. This EWS will allow the country to streamline the capabilities of the emergency and disaster management system at the national level, as well as to make the best decisions in the areas of recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction with a resilient approach. B) Development of the ANR: The Atlas is a comprehensive information system, which allows establishing databases and performing hazard, vulnerability and disaster risk analysis at national, regional, provincial and municipal levels, in order to generate maps and geographic information systems. This Atlas will be developed based on the consolidation of all public information on social, infrastructure, economic and environmental vulnerabilities in each of the country's regions. This will facilitate the management of risks and damages caused by climate change in the country, which in turn will make international financing and private investments available to the country to improve adaptation and resilience to the effects of adverse events.
